Fojas números 1, 2: Mensaje del Poder Ejecutivo número 1.461/01, solicitando acuerdo
Tiene la palabra el señor senador Cafiero.

notes:
13 turns, 4 events. The page opens with a printed label on its first line, so it does not open mid-utterance. The chair speaks six times in a row with only votes, headings and unlabelled run-on paragraphs between; each printed label is listed separately, and the unlabelled indented paragraphs ('Si no se hace uso de la palabra, se va a votar.', 'De esta forma quedan rendidos los homenajes...', 'En todo caso, esta Presidencia le ruega...', 'Se va a votar el pedido de inserción.', and the secretary's 'Fojas números 3, 4, 5...' and 'Fojas 14, 15, 16 y 17 última.') are continuations, not new turns.

The terminator is inconsistent on this one page: the chair is always 'Sr. Presidente (Menem). —' with a space each side of an em dash; the first secretary label is 'Sr. Secretario (Oyarzún).—' with no space before the em dash; the second secretary label, in Asuntos Entrados, is 'Sr. Secretario (Oyarzún).-' with a plain hyphen. All three are recorded exactly as printed.

Case I was unsure about: the centred bold line 'Incorporar S. 1627/01' sits between the secretary's '(Lee:)' label and the chair's next label. It is set like a section heading (centred, bold), so I listed it under headings, but it reads as an unresolved typesetting instruction — a note to insert the text of S. 1627/01 — rather than a real section title, and the text of that resolution never appears on the page. That is the one thing on the page that looks like a typesetting accident. Because of it, the secretary's turn consists only of '(Lee:)': per the brief, '(Lee:)' printed in the same paragraph as the label is part of that turn, not a separate event, so it is the turn's first words and not in the events list.

The four italic dashed lines stand as their own paragraphs and are events. The 'S.1627/01' in the chair's opening paragraph is a bill number inside the speech, not furniture. 'Señor senador:  ya pasó' is printed with two spaces after the colon.
